newsitem.title: FRANCE: RUGBY UNION-TOULOUSE REIGN CONTINUES IN FRANCE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-TOULOUSE REIGN CONTINUES IN FRANCE.

text.p: Toulouse claimed the French championship title for a fourth successive year on Saturday after beating Bourgoin 12-6 in a scrappy final at Parc des Princes.
Former French fly-half Christophe Deylaud landed all Toulouse's points with three penalties and a 71st minute drop goal which effectively settled the outcome.

Bourgoin, winners of the European Conference title this season but appearing in their first French championship final, did their chances little good by turning down a kickable penalty opportunity with five minutes left which would have levelled the scores.
They were never ahead but two penalties from full-back Nigel Geany, a New Zealander working in the French wine trade, kept them in contention right to the end.
The result was a particular disappointment for Bourgoin's former French international forward Marc Cecillon, appearing in his first championship final at the age of 38.
